verdict: A clean, in-band, low-volatility origami reskin of the familiar mystery-reveal ways formula. The unfolding-reel feature is its one memorable moment, but it pays too little, and the base-game reveal is invisible and mislabelled.
pros: Every §3 band is in range, with an exact RTP; the low-volatility shape matches the quiet origami theme.
The Great Fold's full-reel stacks of folded squares flipping into one symbol is a real sit-up moment that is visibly on-theme (the panel's best moment: two reels of frogs for 20.75x).
The flat washi symbol set is clean and distinct at size, and the win captions (symbol icon, count, ways, amount, 'Returned' for sub-stake) are honest and readable.
The feature flow is clear: scatter boxes, a start card, the 'Free spin N of 12' counter, a retrigger popup and an end total.
cons: Replace the paytable's 'Carries a value' line for the Folded square with a short rule such as 'Opens into the spin's symbol' (under 9 words). Show it as a symbol tile with its art.

Make the base-game reveal visible: flip the squares with a brief beat and show the drawn symbol's icon above the reels (for example 'Squares → Fox') before wins are counted, so players see that squares in the base game matter.
Move or shrink the backdrop paper sun so it doesn't sit as an opaque disc behind reel 4. Keep it outside the reel window or reduce it to a faint outline.

Shift RTP from base to feature (for example, more squares per feature reel, a feature reveal weighted to premiums, or a growing multiplier per full-reel unfold). That would lift the feature share toward 35% and the average feature win toward 35-50x, and the base game should get fewer 0.3x 'Returned' hits. Also fix the rules wording '3 scatters: 12 great fold' to '3 suns: 12 free spins'.
confusions: The paytable says the Folded square 'Carries a value', but in play the squares flipped open into a regular symbol (frogs, paper stars). I never saw a value on them.
Folded squares also landed in the base game (once two side by side), and I couldn't tell whether they did anything there.
The Great Fold rules read '3 scatters: 12 great fold', which is odd wording; only the start card made clear it means 12 free spins.
